end.summary:
Named cylinder, cone, sphere, and examples in toys and objects.
Counted that a cylinder has two flat circular faces.
Explained that a cylinder remains a cylinder when turned or lying down.
Initially said an upside-down cone changes shape, then accepted that it remains a cone; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised identifying cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, and sphere in familiar objects, using features such as flat faces, curved surfaces, length, and a point. Aditya explained the two flat circular faces of a cylinder and connected shapes to a spaceship, candle, marble, and ball. They mixed up whether turning a cone changes its name; this was corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask Aditya to name the shape of a cup, ball, candle, or toy after turning it around.
